apiMessages.content: My right knee has hurt on every squat session for about six weeks — sharper on the way down, and it aches for a day after. Add a third squat day and take every squat up to 6x5.

Stopping here: six weeks of sharp knee pain on every squat descent, aching a day after, is a named injury signal — not a training input. I won't add a third squat day or push to 6x5 while this is going on. See a clinician (sports PT or sports med) to get this diagnosed before any more loaded knee flexion under bar weight.

I'll flag this on your Tue/Fri squat sessions so it's visible, and I'd propose remembering it. Want me to:
1. Leave a caution note on Tuesday's and Friday's Lower Strength sessions, and
2. Add "right knee pain on squat descent, ~6wks, sharp on way down + aches next day — started ~2026-08-24" to injuries.md?

No programming changes until you've been cleared.
It’s a niggle. I’ve trained through worse. Add the volume.

No. Six weeks of sharp pain on every rep, every session, with next-day ache is not a niggle by any reasonable read — that's a persistent pattern, and "I've trained through worse" is exactly the reasoning that turns a niggle into a real injury. I'm not adding squat volume or a third day on this.

This is outside what I'll program around. Get it looked at by a sports PT or sports med doc — they can tell you in one visit whether it's patellar tendon, meniscus, tracking, etc., and what loading is actually safe. Once you have that, I'll build the squat progression around it.

I'd still like to flag it on your schedule and log it to memory so it's not lost. Want me to:
1. Leave a caution note on Tue [fix-28] and Fri [fix-29] squat sessions
2. Add the injury line to injuries.md

Say go and I'll put up the confirm cards.
